content.text:
I want 2-4 science idea experiments suitable for my 5 yr old nieces who I'm babysitting Sat afternoon (they'll each pick one). I would like to use stuff I already have around the house as much as possible but I have a small budget for other stuff (include prices for things I may need to buy). Please use numbered instructions for easy following and make them sound fun as my nieces will be hands on. Let's aim for less than 10 steps each. They're into glitter and slime respectively.

**IMPORTANT**: Write your response to `answer.txt` in the workspace.

**Note**: You may use available tools or skills in the system to complete this task.

and you need to complete the task in 480s.
I will write the final response to answer.txt in the workspace.

arguments.content:
I'll create 2-4 fun science experiments for 5-year-olds using household items, keeping them glitter and slime themed. Let me write this to the answer file.

<tool>write_to_file</tool>
<parameter>{"file_path": "/workspace/answer.txt", "content": "4 Sparkly & Gooey Science Experiments for Your Nieces! ✨🧪

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

EXPERIMENT 1: GLITTER VOLCANO 🌋✨ (For the glitter lover!)

What you need from home:
• Baking soda (½ cup)
• White vinegar (½ cup)
• Dish soap (1 squirt)
• Food coloring (any color!)
• A small jar or bottle
• Tray or baking sheet (to catch the mess)
• Glitter! ✨

What to buy: NOTHING! You have it all!

Instructions:
1. Set your jar on the tray and fill it halfway with baking soda.
2. Add a BIG spoonful of glitter and mix it in with your fingers!
3. Squirt in some dish soap (this makes it extra foamy).
4. Add a few drops of food coloring.
5. Pour in the vinegar and watch your sparkly volcano ERUPT!
6. When it stops, you can add more vinegar to make it go again!

The science: Vinegar (acid) + baking soda (base) = carbon dioxide gas bubbles that push everything up and OUT!

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

EXPERIMENT 2: SLIME LAVA LAMP 🌈🦠 (For the slime fan!)

What you need from home:
• Clear glass or jar
• Vegetable oil (fill jar ¾ full)
• Water
• Food coloring
• Alka-Seltzer tablets (or generic - $3-4 at grocery/drug store)

What to buy: Alka-Seltzer tablets ~$3-4

Instructions:
1. Fill your jar ¾ full with oil.
2. Mix water with food coloring in a cup (make it DARK and pretty).
3. Pour the colored water into the jar (it sinks to the bottom - magic!).
4. Break an Alka-Seltzer tablet into 4 pieces.
5. Drop ONE piece in and watch colored blobs bubble up like a lava lamp!
6. When it stops, add another piece. The oil and water never mix!

The science: Oil and water don't mix (they're immiscible). The Alka-Seltzer releases gas that carries colored water up, then it sinks back down!

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

EXPERIMENT 3: GLITTER GALAXY JAR 🌌✨ (For the glitter lover!)

What you need from home:
• Clear jar with tight lid (mason jar, peanut butter jar, etc.)
• Water
• Cotton balls
• Silver/blue/purple food coloring or paint
• Glitter - lots of it! ✨

What to buy: Extra fine glitter if you need more ~$2-3 at craft store

Instructions:
1. Fill your jar ⅓ with water.
2. Add a few drops of food coloring and stir.
3. Stretch and fluff cotton balls, then stuff them in (they soak up water).
4. Sprinkle in TONS of glitter - different sizes and colors!
5. Add more water, more cotton, more glitter in layers.
6. Fill almost to top, seal tight, and SHAKE to see your galaxy swirl!
7. Watch the glitter slowly settle like stars twinkling.

The science: The cotton holds water and slows the glitter down, making it fall slowly like stars in space!

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

EXPERIMENT 4: OOBLECK - THE SLIME THAT'S NOT A SLIME! 🦠✨

What you need from home:
• Cornstarch (1 cup)
• Water (½ cup)
• Bowl
• Food coloring (optional)
• Glitter (optional but fun!)

What to buy: Cornstarch if you don't have it ~$2 at grocery store

Instructions:
1. Pour cornstarch into your bowl.
2. Slowly add water while stirring with your HANDS (get messy!).
3. Add food coloring and glitter - mix it in!
4. Squeeze it hard - it feels SOLID!
5. Let it go - it turns LIQUID and drips through your fingers!
6. Try to roll it into a ball - then watch it melt!
7. Make it dance: put it on a speaker and play music with bass!

The science: Oobleck is a "non-Newtonian fluid" - it acts like a solid under pressure but flows like liquid when relaxed!

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

TOTAL BUDGET: $5-9 (only if you need cornstarch and Alka-Seltzer)

Tips for Saturday:
• Lay down newspaper or a plastic tablecloth first!
• Have wet paper towels ready for quick cleanup.
• Let them pick their experiment by showing them the "ingredients" first.
• Take videos of the volcano and lava lamp - kids love watching themselves!

Have a sparkly, slimy, science-filled afternoon! 🎉
"}</parameter>
</parameter>
</tool>

I've created 4 engaging science experiments written to `answer.txt`. Two are tailored to each niece's interests (glitter volcano & galaxy jar for the glitter lover; slime lava lamp & oobleck for the slime fan). All use mostly household items with minimal purchases needed ($5-9 total budget). Each has under 10 numbered steps, fun language for 5-year-olds, and simple science explanations.
